nodes.label: mount plan
nodes.summary: The configuration handed from the application layer to the kernel, shown feeding the kernel's session in the architecture diagram.

nodes.label: kernel
nodes.summary: amplifier-core; the architecture diagram shows it containing the session and the coordinator.

nodes.label: session
nodes.summary: Kernel component that receives the mount plan and drives the coordinator.

nodes.label: coordinator
nodes.summary: Kernel component below the session that fans out to mounted modules.

nodes.label: event
nodes.summary: Observable occurrences that make everything important observable and decouple emitters from observers.

nodes.label: hook
nodes.summary: Module type through which behavior is added in response to events rather than via code changes.

nodes.label: library
nodes.summary: Supporting libraries provide higher-level functionality and are application-layer concerns.

nodes.label: amplifier-profiles
nodes.summary: Library for profile loading and inheritance.

nodes.label: amplifier-collections
nodes.summary: Library for collection discovery and management.

nodes.label: amplifier-config
nodes.summary: Library for three-scope configuration.

nodes.label: amplifier-module-resolution
nodes.summary: Library for module source resolution.

nodes.label: libraries are not part of the kernel
nodes.summary: Supporting libraries are application-layer concerns, not kernel.

nodes.label: additive first
nodes.summary: Extend contracts without breaking them; prefer optional capabilities.

nodes.label: two-implementation rule
nodes.summary: Don't promote a concept into kernel until two or more independent modules converge on the need.

nodes.label: spec before code
nodes.summary: Kernel changes begin with a short spec covering purpose, alternatives, invariants, tests and rollback.

nodes.label: complexity budget
nodes.summary: Each kernel change must justify its complexity and should retire equivalent complexity elsewhere.

nodes.label: small and sharp interfaces
nodes.summary: Prefer few, precise operations over broad, do-everything calls.

nodes.label: module
nodes.summary: Swappable unit of functionality mounted into the kernel.

nodes.label: provider
nodes.summary: Module type that completes chat requests against an LLM.

nodes.label: observability
nodes.summary: The property that everything important in the system can be observed.

nodes.label: mount function
nodes.summary: Async entry point every module exposes; it receives the coordinator and its config from the mount plan and may return a cleanup function.

nodes.label: cleanup function
nodes.summary: Optional callable returned by a module's mount function to release resources.

nodes.label: capability registry
nodes.summary: Coordinator mechanism by which modules register and look up named capabilities such as a cache.

nodes.label: contribution channel
nodes.summary: Non-interfering aggregation pattern in which modules register contributors and consumers collect their contributions.

nodes.label: module independence
nodes.summary: Modules have no peer awareness, do not crash each other, are swappable and testable in isolation.

nodes.label: tool
nodes.summary: Module type providing capabilities agents can invoke, e.g. tool-filesystem and tool-bash.

nodes.label: agent
nodes.summary: A named configuration with a description, a tool subset and system instructions.

nodes.label: orchestrator
nodes.summary: Module that runs the execution loop, e.g. loop-streaming.

nodes.label: context manager
nodes.summary: Module that holds conversation context, e.g. context-persistent.

nodes.label: if it's important, emit an event
nodes.summary: Event-system design principle: anything important must be emitted as an event.

nodes.label: if it's not observable, it didn't happen
nodes.summary: Event-system design principle equating unobservable actions with non-events.

nodes.label: events.jsonl
nodes.summary: Per-session JSONL event log, the single source of truth for events.

nodes.label: hooks observe without blocking
nodes.summary: Hooks observe events without blocking, by default.

nodes.label: session:fork
nodes.summary: Canonical event emitted when a sub-session is created, carrying parent_id and child_id.

nodes.label: provider:request
nodes.summary: Canonical event emitted before an LLM call.

nodes.label: tool:pre
nodes.summary: Canonical event emitted before tool execution.

nodes.label: namespace:action convention
nodes.summary: Custom events follow the namespace:action naming convention.

nodes.label: trace context
nodes.summary: Tracing identifiers session_id, request_id and span_id included in events.

nodes.label: sub-session
nodes.summary: A child session spawned by an agent, whose session_id is derived from the parent's.

nodes.label: log level
nodes.summary: Logging verbosity levels from warn through raw, where raw adds complete API payloads.

nodes.label: researcher
nodes.summary: Bundled agent for research and information synthesis, including web search and source citation.

nodes.label: modular-builder
nodes.summary: Bundled agent for focused code implementation.

nodes.label: zen-architect
nodes.summary: Bundled agent for design, refactoring decisions and architecture review.

nodes.label: profile
nodes.summary: YAML-frontmatter configuration that can extend another profile and define agents.

nodes.label: standalone agent file
nodes.summary: An agent defined in its own markdown file under .amplifier/agents/.

nodes.label: conversation history
nodes.summary: The user's prompts and AI responses recorded in a session.

nodes.label: session resumption
nodes.summary: Continuing a previous session via amplifier continue or amplifier session resume.

nodes.label: context limit
nodes.summary: The model's maximum context, which a resumed conversation history may exceed.

nodes.label: session event type list
nodes.summary: The sessions guide's table of seven event types found in a session's events.jsonl.

nodes.label: collection
nodes.summary: A shareable package of profiles, agents and context, published via a git repository.

nodes.label: semantic versioning
nodes.summary: Collections use vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, with major for breaking changes.

nodes.label: context file
nodes.summary: Markdown guidance in a collection's context/ directory referenced from profiles with @context/.

nodes.label: profile inheritance
nodes.summary: A child profile extends a parent, inheriting all settings, overriding some and adding system instructions.

nodes.label: inheritance never removes parent features
nodes.summary: Claim that each level of the inheritance chain adds capabilities without removing parent features.

nodes.label: profile-specific tools
nodes.summary: Enabling or disabling tools per profile, e.g. a safe-profile with read-only filesystem and tool-bash omitted.

nodes.label: system instruction
nodes.summary: The markdown body after a profile's frontmatter, which becomes the system instruction.

nodes.label: model provider
nodes.summary: An LLM vendor configured for Amplifier, such as Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI or Ollama.

nodes.label: settings.yaml
nodes.summary: ~/.amplifier/settings.yaml, an alternative configuration file for providers such as Azure.

nodes.label: tool contract
nodes.summary: Protocol requiring a tool to have name, description and an async execute(input) returning ToolResult.

nodes.label: toolresult
nodes.summary: Result of a tool execution with success, output, error and metadata fields.

nodes.label: input_schema
nodes.summary: JSON Schema of tool parameters, commonly implemented but not part of the formal Tool protocol.

nodes.label: hookresult
nodes.summary: Value returned by a hook handler, whose action is one of continue, deny, modify, inject_context or ask_user.

nodes.label: hook handler registration
nodes.summary: Hooks register handlers for events with a priority instead of mounting into a slot.

nodes.label: deny action
nodes.summary: HookResult action that blocks the operation with a reason.

nodes.label: inject_context action
nodes.summary: HookResult action that adds content to the conversation, e.g. linter findings.

nodes.label: ask_user action
nodes.summary: HookResult action that requests user approval with options and a default.

nodes.label: agent loop
nodes.summary: Orchestrator loop that calls the provider, executes requested tools, appends results to context, and stops at max iterations.

nodes.label: context truncation
nodes.summary: Context strategy that keeps system messages and drops oldest other messages until under 70% of max tokens.

nodes.label: token estimate
nodes.summary: Rough token estimate of 4 characters per token.

nodes.label: persistent context
nodes.summary: Context implementation that saves messages to a storage path for session resumption.

nodes.label: context contract
nodes.summary: Authoritative context specification kept in amplifier-core.

nodes.label: learning from sessions
nodes.summary: Roadmap idea: tools to parse session data and analyze patterns so the system improves from accumulated experience.

nodes.label: smart tool
nodes.summary: A library with wrappers around it, where the library holds the capability and every other surface is a thin adapter.

nodes.label: the library is the tool
nodes.summary: Everything the tool can do is reachable from the library; no capability exists only in a wrapper.

nodes.label: wrapper
nodes.summary: A thin adapter (CLI, MCP server, web service) exposing the library's capability in a different shape.

nodes.label: wrapper removal test
nodes.summary: Test of whether removing a wrapper would lose anything a different caller might want.

nodes.label: caller adapter
nodes.summary: An adapter callers put in front of the library to constrain the surface they depend on.

nodes.label: manifest
nodes.summary: SMART_TOOL.md: a single file shipped with the tool saying what it is, what it is for, and what it needs to run.

nodes.label: selection, not operation
nodes.summary: The manifest answers whether this is the right tool and whether it runs here, not how to call it.

nodes.label: cached manifest snapshot
nodes.summary: An exact generated copy of a manifest a catalog may cache with source, revision, path and refresh time recorded.

nodes.label: catalog
nodes.summary: Catalogs and registries that consume manifests from the canonical upstream source.

nodes.label: manifest schema version
nodes.summary: Manifest field giving the schema version, not the tool's version, so readers know whether they understand the file.

nodes.label: single version source
nodes.summary: The manifest version must match the package definition version; three different answers to one question means consumers eventually pick the wrong one.

nodes.label: manifest description
nodes.summary: Field saying what the tool does and when to reach for it, read by users and by agents deciding routing.

nodes.label: use_cases
nodes.summary: Concrete jobs the tool is for, as selection aids rather than a capability list.

nodes.label: platforms
nodes.summary: Operating systems the tool actually works on, not those it theoretically compiles for.

nodes.label: self-description
nodes.summary: A smart tool's ability to describe its own surface: capabilities, arguments, types and returns.

nodes.label: -h summary
nodes.summary: Terse, scannable user summary listing capabilities with one line each.

nodes.label: --help skill
nodes.summary: Agent-facing help shaped like an Agent Skill, read once the agent has decided to use the tool.

nodes.label: skill
nodes.summary: Agent Skill format as a host delivers it to a model.

nodes.label: result provenance transparency
nodes.summary: A caller should not need to know whether a result came from code, a model, or both to use it correctly.

nodes.label: ai-enabled capability disclosure
nodes.summary: Docs and help should make clear which functionality is AI-enabled, stated explicitly if ambiguous.

nodes.label: tool name
nodes.summary: Manifest name field, lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens, the tool's identity across registry, package index and CLI.

nodes.label: context payload
nodes.summary: Optional extra material a caller already has, passed to a smart tool to help it do the job well.

nodes.label: payload is data, not a reference
nodes.summary: At the library level callers pass actual content, not paths, keeping the library free of filesystem assumptions.

nodes.label: mechanical context assembly
nodes.summary: Whatever selects and packages context should be caller-controlled code, not an agent's judgment of relevance.

nodes.label: context granularity
nodes.summary: None, partial and full as the useful granularity of how much context the caller hands over.

nodes.label: tool-driven working directory access
nodes.summary: A tool's own intelligence may use the working directory via tools like read and bash as another means of context.

nodes.label: git installation
nodes.summary: Installing a smart tool from a git repository, the one method every tool must support.

nodes.label: ecosystem registry
nodes.summary: Optional publishing target such as pypi, npm, cargo, oci or go.

nodes.label: install script
nodes.summary: Permitted where setup is more than placing a package; installs the tool and nothing else.

nodes.label: runner
nodes.summary: How a published tool is started once obtained, e.g. uvx, npx, docker; absent when a binary lands on the path.

nodes.label: descriptor
nodes.summary: smart-tool.json at the distribution root, stating where the manifest sits and how the tool is started.
